# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

# gh-862: [BUG] gh-857's conclude never fires: latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe — ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt (live: fa #1457, two ticks on rel-204928)

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

## References

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

## References

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

# gh-862: [BUG] gh-857's conclude never fires: latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe — ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt (live: fa #1457, two ticks on rel-204928)

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

## References

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===

# gh-862: [BUG] gh-857's conclude never fires: latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe — ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt (live: fa #1457, two ticks on rel-204928)

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

## References

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===
./js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
./js/smAgent.js

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). 1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

# gh-862: [BUG] gh-857's conclude never fires: latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe — ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt (live: fa #1457, two ticks on rel-204928)

## Description

## Live

gh-857's placeholder-conclude fix (PR #858, released in agents-rel-20261011-204928) is deployed but NEVER FIRES. Two consecutive SM ticks on rel-204928 (fa runs 38174670336 @21:01Z, 38174907277 @21:06Z) processed the pinned PR (fa #1457, head fd1b9aa2, green, ai_validated, gate BLOCKED by an in_progress placeholder from 18:51:25) and the logs show only: 'stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch' + the legacy stamp POSTs (factory #510 mode). NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt.

Suspect: for a PR with ai_validated already latched and an unchanged head, the latch-skip 'arm only' path returns before the merge-validated probe stage — so the conclude (placed in the probe) and the merge itself are unreachable for exactly the PRs that need them most. The merge window must run for ai_validated-latched PRs regardless of head-change.

## Goal

Fix the stage ordering in the SM reconcile: the merge-validated probe (placeholder conclude + merge attempt) must execute for every PR carrying ai_validated with a green verdict — including latch-skip 'arm only' heads. Add a regression probe to the agents unit suite: ai_validated + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires and merge is attempted in the same tick.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: fa #1457 (or any placeholder-pinned ai_validated PR) merges within one tick without operator action.
2. AC2: unit test covers the latch-skip → probe ordering (the gap that shipped #857 unfireable).

## References

gh-857 (the conclude fix that landed but never runs), gh-848 (placeholder law, 9 live instances), fa tick logs 38174670336/38174907277.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===
./js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js
./js/smAgent.js

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
===

/**
 * Check-run zombies (gh-842) — the gate-ghost classifier.
 *
 * Live fa #1457 (2026-10-10, head 7d00a1b2, ~14:30→16:00Z): a dispatched CI
 * run was CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard family) and later ceased
 * to exist; the `in_progress` check runs it had registered on the head were
 * never concluded. Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per
 * (context, head), so the ghosts held mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h even
 * though the head ALSO carried terminal GREEN entries from the earlier run
 * 38057801418 (green, 13:58). The tick's green-cover guard (skipIfGreenCi)
 * read the surviving green run as covering the head — "the blocker is not
 * this CI" — and never re-dispatched; the window idled until an operator
 * nudged a fresh dispatch. The gh-821 zombie sweep missed it because the
 * dispatched-RUN probe reads green (the newest EXISTING run is the old
 * green one) — gh-821 classifies runs, gh-842 classifies the check-RUN
 * ghosts those dead runs leave on the gate.
 *
 * This module is the pure half of the fix:
 *
 *   classify(checkRuns, resolveRun, nowMs, opts)
 *                      — partition a head's check-runs: every PENDING
 *                      (queued/in_progress, no conclusion) check-run whose
 *                      backing workflow run is ABSENT (deleted/404),
 *                      concluded CANCELLED, concluded non-cancelled past a
 *                      short propagation grace, or link-less and stale past
 *                      the no-runner threshold, is a ZOMBIE. Everything
 *                      else — concluded checks, live runs, fresh stamps,
 *                      probe errors — is LIVE (AC2: a genuinely in-progress
 *                      run is NEVER disturbed; every unprovable case fails
 *                      SAFE toward live, a missed zombie retries next tick
 *                      while a wrongful re-dispatch burns CI).
 *   runIdOf(checkRun)  — the backing workflow-run id parsed out of
 *                      details_url/html_url (`/actions/runs/<id>`); bridge
 *                      stamps dispatched without a run URL carry none.
 *
 * A zombie's context counts as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) in the caller: the
 * surviving evidence decides the real rollup, and the caller re-dispatches
 * validation so the fresh stamps become the LATEST per context and override
 * the ghosts on the gate.
 *
 * Pure functions, no tool globals — smAgent wires the transport (the
 * bridge check-runs tool + the head run list as the resolver's source),
 * tests inject nothing. CommonJS module like every other js/ module.
 * GraalJS rules apply: var + plain functions only.
 */

# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.

{"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.

{"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

{"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.

{"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. {"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.

{"content":"# gh-862 RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: gh-857's placeholder-conclude never fires and ai_validated PRs with unchanged heads never get a merge attempt — the latch-skip "arm only" path returns before the merge-validated probe.

**Root cause**: `js/smAgent.js`, `validate_pr` action, latch-skip arm-only branch (~line 2116-2123). When the latch-skip arms `ai_validating` without a dispatch, it does `processedKeys.push(key); continue;` — the merge-validated probe (gh-857 placeholder conclude + merge attempt) is never executed for that PR in the tick. In the deployed rule order (`sm_github.json`) `merge-validated` (index 6) runs BEFORE `validate-armed` (index 11), so the arm always lands after the merge window has already queried. The arm is then eaten by `sweep-stale-validating` (index 8) on the next tick ("stale arm swept"), re-armed by the latch-skip, and so on — the live fa #1457 ping-pong: two consecutive ticks logged only `stale arm swept → latch-skip (arm only) → head already carries a green dispatched CI run, skip re-dispatch`, with NO conclude action, NO merge-validated probe line, NO merge attempt. The gh-857 conclude (in the placeholder gate of the same `validate_pr` action) sits past the latch-skip `continue`, unreachable for exactly these PRs; and even where the conclude does fire (placeholder gate), the branch continues without attempting the merge in the same tick.

**Impact**: Any PR carrying `ai_validated` with an unchanged green head and a gate blocker (placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run pinning mergeState BLOCKED) never merges without operator action — the merge window is unreachable from the arm-only path and the conclude is unreachable from the latch-skip skip.

**Fix approach**: Extract the merge attempt from the `merge_pr` action into a shared `attemptMergeProbe` helper and invoke it (1) in the latch-skip arm-only branch right after arming, and (2) in the gh-857 conclude-success branch right after the placeholders are concluded — so the placeholder conclude + merge attempt execute in the same tick for every PR carrying `ai_validated` with a green verdict, regardless of head-change. A refused merge keeps the markers (self-heal via merge-validated next tick), preserving fa pr-753 semantics.

**Regression probe (AC2)**: `ai_validated` + unchanged head + placeholder-shaped in_progress check-run → conclude PATCH fires AND merge is attempted in the same tick; plus the pure arm-only shape (no placeholders) → merge attempted in the same tick as the arm.
